summary: Independently verified TripShield security fixes (SEC-001 dealer gate, SEC-002 IDOR on journey endpoints, SEC-004 public-track hardening) plus cross-user isolation on documents/contacts/journeys/incidents/claims and the owner happy-path regression. 20/20 pytest checks pass against the public preview URL.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 755 lines and mixes all domains (auth, vehicle, documents, contacts, geo, journeys, incidents, claims, dealer). Consider splitting into routers per domain for maintainability.

SEC-001 login allowlist (DEALER_EMAILS) cannot be exercised via seeded Mongo sessions; verified by code inspection at ~L94-99 and by confirming dealer endpoints 403 for user tokens / 200 for seeded dealer session. Recommend adding an integration test once test OAuth harness is available.

public_track still exposes user_name, from_name, to_name and 'arrived' event data for completed journeys — confirm this residual disclosure is intentional per product spec (route/live position are now suppressed which was the stated fix).

POST /journeys/{id}/position (line 440) does not validate ownership on the update filter alone — the update is a no-op for a non-owner (silent no-match), which is safe but should probably 404 for consistency with sibling endpoints.

POST /claims does not verify that the referenced journey_id/incident_id belong to the caller before embedding their data into the claim package (lines 579-599). Not exercised in current threat model but is an IDOR-adjacent risk.

seed_data_creation: Tests create ephemeral vehicles, journeys, documents, contacts, incidents and claims prefixed with TEST_ under both user A and user B; no cleanup performed (test data is small and non-destructive).
context_for_next_testing_agent: pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_security.py covers SEC-001/002/004 + isolation + owner regression using seeded tokens. Runs in ~3s in parallel (pytest-xdist). Base URL comes from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. If new endpoints are added, extend TestOwnershipIsolation with same pattern (create as A & B, assert disjoint IDs).
rca of the issue: N/A — no regressions detected. Two initial test failures were due to my test payloads not matching backend Pydantic schemas (DocumentIn expects doc_type/doc_number; ClaimIn requires insurer). Fixed in test file; app behavior is correct.
